_meta.note: Four complementary how-to files for the behavioral-gates guide, same dogfooded approach: every claim backed by a runnable proof + adversarially refuted by a distinct actor. New runnable proofs reuse the existing self-verifying runner where possible. RG0 extends the example corpus to NON-CODE deliverables (a document, a dataset) proven by the same run.sh triple. RG1 adds two mechanism demos that drive the REAL runtime: refutation-demo.sh drives the public hb CLI review guard (pass needs a substantive, anchored artifact from a DIFFERENT actor); fast-determinism-check.sh proves the corpus is deterministic across runs and completes well under a time budget. RG2 writes the four docs (10 rules, add refutation, fast+deterministic, non-code), wires them into the index + main guide, and enforces the new proofs in the node suite (T54) so they cannot rot.

tasks.title: Note non-code deliverables in the spec
tasks.description: Spec-first: extend docs/howto/gate-examples/SPEC.md to note that an example's artifact need not be code — a document or dataset deliverable uses the same discriminating triple (stub / weak_gate / strong_gate).

tasks.title: Author the non-code examples
tasks.description: Add docs/howto/gate-examples/non-code-doc/ (a report.md whose Recommendation section must have real content, not a TODO placeholder) and docs/howto/gate-examples/non-code-data/ (a data.csv that must parse to the right schema with at least one valid row) — each a self-contained example proven by docs/howto/gate-examples/run.sh, no model.

tasks.title: Refutation guard demo
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/refutation-demo.sh: bootstrap a throwaway project via the public hb CLI, drive a review-gated phase to review_pending, and assert the real guard — a pass is rejected with no --artifact, rejected for a thin/anchorless artifact, rejected for a self-review (same HB_ACTOR as the doer), and accepted only for a substantive, phase-anchored artifact from a DIFFERENT actor. Print REFUTATION-GUARDS-OK when all four hold.

tasks.title: Fast + deterministic demo
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/fast-determinism-check.sh: run docs/howto/gate-examples/run.sh twice and assert byte-identical output (deterministic: same artifacts, same verdict), and assert the whole corpus completes under a generous time budget via timeout (fast, not a flaky tight bound). Print FAST-DETERMINISTIC-OK when both hold.

tasks.description: Write docs/howto/writing-gates-10-rules.md (ten numbered rules, each pointing at a runnable proof in gate-examples/ or a sibling how-to; a checklist that links, not a fourth copy of the enforced rules) and docs/howto/add-refutation-to-a-sensitive-gate.md (how to add a review block; its proof is refutation-demo.sh).

Follow the project doc rules (current-state, no archeology); link the enforced rules rather than restating them.

tasks.title: Index, cross-link, enforce

GATE_RG0.desc: Non-code deliverables are gated behaviorally: the same runner proves a document and a dataset example, weak gate fooled, behavioral gate rejects the placeholder/wrong-shape stub.

review.prompt: Refute that RG0 is done: is either non-code strong_gate really behavioral, or existence in disguise (does non-code-doc's strong gate actually reject a TODO placeholder, and non-code-data's reject a header-only CSV)? Does the weak gate genuinely pass on the stub? Are both proven by the shared runner?

criteria.desc: the runner proves every example including the new ones
both non-code examples are proven by name
criteria.cmd: out=$(bash "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/gate-examples/run.sh" 2>&1); for e in non-code-doc non-code-data; do printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "^PROVEN:$e$" || exit 1; done

GATE_RG1.desc: Both mechanism demos drive the real runtime and report their markers.

review.prompt: Refute that RG1 is done: does refutation-demo.sh drive the REAL hb CLI review guard (not a mock), and does it actually check all four outcomes (no-artifact / thin / self-review / distinct-actor)? Does fast-determinism-check.sh really re-run and diff two runs and enforce a timeout, or is the marker cosmetic?

GATE_RG2.desc: Each doc points at a proof that runs; the index and main guide link them; the suite enforces the demos.

review.prompt: Refute that RG2 is done: does any doc claim a proof that does not run? Is writing-gates-10-rules.md a fourth copy of the enforced rules that will drift, rather than a checklist that links them? Is any of the four docs missing from the index or unlinked from the main guide? Does T54 actually enforce the demos?

criteria.desc: each doc references its runnable proof
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto" && grep -q 'refutation-demo' add-refutation-to-a-sensitive-gate.md && grep -q 'fast-determinism-check' write-fast-deterministic-gates.md && grep -q 'non-code-doc' write-gates-for-non-code-work.md && grep -q 'non-code-data' write-gates-for-non-code-work.md && grep -q 'gate-examples' writing-gates-10-rules.md

criteria.desc: the index lists all four docs
criteria.cmd: for f in writing-gates-10-rules add-refutation-to-a-sensitive-gate write-fast-deterministic-gates write-gates-for-non-code-work; do grep -q "$f" "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/README.md" || exit 1; done
